reason: Conversation 1 went straight to the sensible first step (an independent oven thermometer at 180C with a full preheat), then used the neon-cycling clue when the user had no thermometer and escalated correctly to an engineer, explaining that the exact model number isn't needed for the engineer to proceed. Conversation 2 wasted several turns on low-value checks (looking for a glowing element in a fan oven, a vague 'hand at the door' heat test it kept pressing the user to repeat) and pushed the model-number/parts panel three times for a component the user couldn't fit anyway, taking seven turns to reach the same engineer recommendation. Both were overconfident in calling it a 'classic' failing thermostat and neither asked about preheating or shelf position; Conversation 2 at least noted the flattened seal, but only because the user volunteered it, which doesn't outweigh its inefficiency.
